messages:
nisha: Quick pass on Metrics table row actions — noticed a few accessibility rough edges when tabbing through rows.

ben: thanks, drop repros and I'll patch.

nisha: Repro: Dashboard -> Metrics -> tab into table -> each row has a hidden 'actions' menu that appears on hover. keyboard focus lands on cells but not the actions button, so you can't open row actions via keyboard.

rowan: we probably rely on hover-only CSS to show the button. That's bad.

ben: confirm. CSS .row:hover .actions { opacity:1; pointer-events:auto; } but .actions is not focusable by default.

nisha: fixes: always render actions button in DOM, visually hide it off-screen but make it focusable (use .visually-hidden-focusable pattern). add aria-controls to link to contextual menu and aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded toggled on open.

rowan: agree. snippet: <button class="actions-btn visually-hidden-focusable" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="row-42-menu">More</button>

ben: also need to ensure when menu opens focus moves into the menu and on close it returns to the actions button. we'll use our focus-trap util.

nisha: another issue: screen reader reads each cell twice because we use role="grid" and also ARIA labels on each cell. recommend simple semantic <table> markup and use scope and caption for summary. Avoid role=grid unless full keyboard grid behavior implemented.

rowan: good catch. switching back to native table reduces SR verbosity.

nisha: contrast nit: the action icon color on light theme is ~3.2:1 small size. needs >=3:1 for small UI text/icons per WCAG. propose using var(--icon-contrast) token.

ben: will update token and add storybook examples showing keyboard-only interactions.

a11y-bot: scan report: found 2 focus order issues and 1 contrast failure in staging/table-rows. Axe rule ids: focus-order, color-contrast.

nisha: thanks bot. Ben, can you add test steps in the PR and tag @nisha for quick verification?

ben: yup ETA tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

rowan: i'll update the design tokens and add accessible icon variants.

nisha: great teamwork — this will make row-level actions much more discoverable for keyboard and screen reader users.
